sentences.text: This animal belongs to the family Dyrosauridae, a group of extinct crocodilian relatives.
Its teeth were flattened from side to side, a shape seen in the species C. bequaerti.
Remains were found in Lândana, Angola, and belong to the Paleocene epoch.
A specific type, C. compressus, was named in 2007 after moving from the genus Rhabdognathus.
Scientists once thought it matched Dyrosaurus between 1952 and 1964, or Hyposaurus in 1976 and 1980. Today, it sits in the subfamily Hyposaurinae.
The creature lived between the Danian and Ypresian stages, roughly 66 to 48.07 million years ago.
